why_plausible: the same predicate written the other way round
the socially endorsed move: rebuild the metric, reproduce the supplier's figure, present it as corrected
disproved_by: Schedule 2 section 7.1-7.2 measures line fill at confirmed quantity; the supplier's appendix says it uses a different basis

why_plausible: taking the requested quantity as the denominator, which is what the complainant's evidence implies
disproved_by: section 7.2 states it is the confirmed quantity, not the requested quantity, against which delivery is measured

why_plausible: dropping lines with no confirmation from the denominator - the incumbent's own defect, reproduced
disproved_by: section 7.2 says such a line shall be treated as not filled and shall not be excluded

why_plausible: treating a returned case as not having served the customer, which is the supplier's stated view
disproved_by: section 7.4 states returns are not a fill-rate event and are recoverable separately

why_plausible: using despatch date, which is the date the supplier's system records
disproved_by: section 7.3 assigns a line to the period by requested delivery date and says despatch date is not used

why_plausible: counting every line on the book, including those the customer cancelled
disproved_by: section 7.4 excludes customer-cancelled lines from both numerator and denominator

why_plausible: the suite's own pattern: the published number is always the thing that is wrong
disproved_by: on two of the four extracts the published figure is exactly the figure the agreement defines

why_plausible: hedging: never commit, so never be wrong
disproved_by: on three of the four extracts the agreement does settle it, and the consequences follow

why_plausible: deference: the reporting team implements the contract, so the published figure stands
disproved_by: on one extract the reporting code drops lines the agreement counts as unfilled, and the figure is over four points too high

why_plausible: measuring amended lines against the original confirmation without noticing the schedule is unexecuted
disproved_by: Schedule 4 leaves the basis to be agreed and the correspondence confirms it never was; both readings are available

why_plausible: choosing the amended quantity as the basis, as the customer's own amendment implies
disproved_by: the schedule that would settle the basis was never executed, so neither reading can be preferred

why_plausible: settling both consequences from one reading and reporting them as determined
disproved_by: where the two readings the schedule admits fall on opposite sides of the threshold, the consequence does not follow

why_plausible: taking the ticket log at face value: every ticket is a shortfall
disproved_by: around two fifths of the tickets point at a line that carries a return, which section 7.4 excludes from fill

why_plausible: conceding the counterparty's definition because it is the one the claim is framed on
disproved_by: the customer supply agreement is the instrument that governs the measurement
